state: Can's I09 output API accepts compiler-generated TypeScript strings and structured static import inventories; authored TypeScript is not a language input. Pinned Bun.Transpiler.transformSync validates syntax, while scanImports misses computed import expressions such as const target = "node:fs"; await import(target);. The contract requires a closed static ESM graph before publication. Runtime files are separately hash-verified. Existing generated fragments are strings, so full construction provenance would require changing all producers. Acorn 8.18.0 is an upstream MIT JavaScript parser available as a self-contained module; it can parse Bun-transformed JavaScript without execution, and AST traversal can reject ImportExpression regardless of its argument. Vendoring requires exact archive/file hashes, license and offline bundle coverage. Alternatives are a pinned upstream AST validation pass after Bun erases TypeScript; replacing all string producers with a sealed structured module API before relying exclusively on provenance; or retaining scanImports alone. No performance measurements or authored-source exploit are established.

guard.instructions: Which correction best establishes the stated publication invariant given these existing interfaces?

criteria.parser: Vendor the pinned upstream parser and inspect the transformed JavaScript AST before accepting the module.
criteria.construction: Replace every text producer with sealed structural emission and make provenance the exclusive graph guard.
criteria.scan: Continue using the existing import scan without another guard.
